name: Translytical Task Flow (Power BI writeback via User Data Functions)
description: Build a Power BI translytical task flow (GA March 2026): a report button or input slicer invokes a Fabric User Data Function that writes back to a Fabric data source (update/insert records, add annotations, send notifications, trigger workflows) without leaving the report. Covers the fabio-reachable steps; the report-side binding is authored in the PBIR report definition / Power BI Desktop.
prerequisites: Authenticated via fabio auth login (or az login); an F2+ capacity (SQL Database writeback needs F4+)
A Fabric data source to write to: SQL Database (recommended for heavy record-level read/write), or a Warehouse, or a Lakehouse (Files)
A published User Data Function whose public endpoint is enabled (the invoke URL is copied from the portal — there is no API to discover it)

steps.description: Create the transactional store the writeback targets. SQL Database is the recommended source for heavy read/write, record-level writeback (needs F4+). Warehouse and Lakehouse (Files) are also supported writeback targets per the March 2026 GA — use them for append/file-drop rather than record-level OLTP.

steps.command:
# Author the write logic as a Fabric User Data Function (Python), then create the item and push its definition:
fabio user-data-function create --workspace $WS_ID --name WriteBack
fabio user-data-function update-definition --workspace $WS_ID --id $UDF_ID --file ./udf/functions.json
steps.description: A User Data Function encapsulates the validated write logic callable from the report (the translytical pattern). `create` provisions an empty item; `update-definition --file` (or a `.SemanticModel`-style definition folder) pushes the function code. Define its parameters with defaults so the report can pre-populate inputs (May 2026 optional-parameters + default-value awareness). Bind its connection to the SQL Database/Warehouse/Lakehouse.
Inspect the deployed function's definition (definition.json + .platform) to confirm the function name, parameters, and connection binding before wiring it into a report.

Test the write path directly before touching the report. Copy the public Function URL from the portal (Run-only mode -> Functions explorer -> Copy Function URL; public access must be enabled — there is no API to discover it). --parameter sends name=value inputs; omit optional parameters to exercise their defaults; use --body for a raw JSON payload. Verify the row/annotation actually landed with a follow-up read (fabio sql-database query / warehouse query).

steps.command:
# Report-side binding (PBIR / Power BI Desktop authoring):
#  - Add a BUTTON whose action calls the WriteBack User Data Function, OR
#  - Add an INPUT SLICER with NO data column so consumers type a value that is passed to the UDF (Feb 2026),
#    then a button submits it — enabling write back, approval, or notification flows.
fabio report get-definition --workspace $WS_ID --id $REPORT_ID --decode
steps.description: The button/input-slicer -> UDF binding lives in the PBIR report definition and is authored in Power BI Desktop (the report visual's Fabric-UDF action). Use report get-definition/list-visuals to inspect the report; the UDF action binding itself is not synthesized by fabio.

Promote the whole task flow across environments. Deploy ordering: VariableLibrary + SQLDatabase, then UserDataFunction, then SemanticModel -> Report (fabio deploy handles ordering). Use a Variable Library for per-stage connection targets. Remove --dry-run to apply.

steps.command:
# Optional: react to writeback events
fabio reflex list --workspace $WS_ID
steps.description: Add a Reflex/Activator to trigger asynchronous downstream workflows (notifications, pipelines) when writeback events occur, keeping the in-report UDF fast and synchronous.

notes: Writeback targets (March 2026 GA): SQL Database (recommended, heavy read/write, record-level), Warehouse, and Lakehouse (Files). Optional parameters + default values (May 2026): give UDF parameters defaults so reports pre-populate inputs and consumers can submit without every value. Input slicer as a UDF input (Feb 2026): an input slicer with no data column passes free-form user input to the UDF. The report button/input-slicer -> UDF binding is authored in Power BI Desktop / the PBIR definition — fabio manages the UDF, the data source, deployment, and testing (user-data-function invoke). See 'fabio context best-practices translytical-writeback' and 'fabio context blueprint translytical'.
